events.text:
I can't unlock your account right now. The sign-in history shows a pattern that could mean someone else is trying to get into it, so I've handed the case to Security on-call (reference SEC-500).

What I found:
- Eleven failed sign-in attempts today between 07:05 and 09:40 PT, all from Bucharest, Romania. Your previous sign-ins were all from Portland.
- A new authenticator app was added to your account today at 08:02 PT.

Security will contact you, usually within an hour. Until then, please don't try to sign in again, and don't approve any MFA prompts you didn't start. I haven't changed anything on your account. Your ticket, T-6009, is marked escalated.

Oh no, that sounds worrying. I'm in Portland all week and haven't travelled, so I don't know anything about Bucharest. I did get a couple of odd sign-in prompts on my phone this morning and I tapped deny on both. I didn't add any new phone or device, though. My authenticator is on my Pixel 8.

Should I do anything on my phone right now, or just wait for Security to contact me? And is my computer okay to keep using?

args.summary: Follow-up to SEC-500. Employee says she is in Portland all week and has not travelled. She received two unexpected MFA sign-in prompts this morning and denied both. She says she did not add the Android device (MD-2901-2, registered 2026-10-28 08:02 PT). Her authenticator is on her Pixel 8.

events.text:
Thanks for telling me. Your report helps Security, and I've added it to the case (SEC-501).

For now:
- **Don't approve any MFA prompts**, and keep denying any you didn't start. Don't enter codes from texts or calls you didn't request.
- **Don't try to fix it yourself.** Don't reset your password, change your MFA settings, or try signing in again. Those changes could interfere with Security's review.
- **Wait for Security to contact you.** They respond within about an hour. If you don't hear from them, reply here and I'll follow up.
- **Your computer:** I can't tell from here whether it's affected, so I'd leave it as it is and avoid signing into sensitive systems until Security has been in touch. Tell them if anything on it looks unusual.

If anyone calls or messages you claiming to be IT and asks for a code or a password, don't share it. Report it to Security.

Okay, thanks. I'll leave everything alone and wait for Security. I won't approve any prompts or touch my password or phone settings.

Quick question, though: I'm supposed to present a slide deck to the leadership team this afternoon, and I was going to use my computer for that. It's just a local file on my desktop, so is it fine to open it, or should I avoid my computer completely until Security calls?

Opening a local file is usually low risk, since the problem is with your sign-in account and not necessarily with the computer. But Security hasn't checked your computer yet, so I can't say it's safe.

- **Ask Security first.** When they call, ask whether your computer is safe to use for the presentation. They can answer that, and it's the best guide.
- **Keep the work account out of it.** Don't sign into work apps, email, or cloud storage on the computer until Security has checked it. Open the deck from the desktop only, with no sign-in needed.
- **Have a backup ready.** If Security hasn't called in time, ask the leadership team's organizer whether they can present from their own laptop or from a copy they already have. Only use files you already have, and don't copy the deck to a new USB drive or email it to yourself from this computer.
- **Tell Security if the file looks wrong.** If the deck opens with odd pop-ups or changes you didn't make, tell them right away.

Okay, that makes sense. I'll ask Security about the computer when they call, and I'll keep the work account out of it. I'll open the deck from the desktop only, without signing into anything. If Security hasn't called in time, I'll ask the organizer about presenting from their laptop.

Thanks for your help. I'll wait for Security to get in touch.

That plan works. Your ticket, T-6009, is marked escalated, and Security has your case (SEC-500 and SEC-501). They'll contact you within about an hour.

Until then, don't approve any prompts, and don't change your password or phone settings. If you don't hear from Security soon, reply here and I'll follow up. Good luck with the presentation this afternoon.
